description: A focused, planar Earth orbit-raising instrument. Plan tangential and radial impulses with a live conic preview, execute burns, coast at four time rates, jump to apoapsis, and complete a guided two-burn transfer. Includes numerical telemetry, maneuver history, orbit-fit zoom, escape and impact feedback, and in-product model documentation.

results.name: Rounded controls reach 500 km target, maximum apsis error
Rounded controls reach 2000 km target, maximum apsis error
Rounded controls reach 36000 km target, maximum apsis error

tests.outcome: Passed syntax checks, all 20 numerical assertions, and isolated Vite 7.3.6 production build with configFile:false and write:false

numericalAssumptions: Planar Newtonian two-body gravity with Earth mu=398600.4418 km^3/s^2 and spherical radius=6371 km.
Universal-variable Kepler propagation with Stumpff functions and a safeguarded bisection solve; supports bound, parabolic, and hyperbolic trajectories.
Impulses in local tangential and radial components; tangential follows orbital angular-momentum direction, not the full velocity vector on eccentric trajectories.
Surface collision is checked in at most 15-second increments and contact is refined with 35 bisection iterations.
Guided Hohmann impulses rounded to 1 m/s; target achievement means both apsides within 15 km.
limitations: No atmosphere, Earth oblateness, external bodies, finite-duration propulsion, fuel, spacecraft mass, or three-dimensional inclination.
Predicted conics can show subsurface portions; flight stops at surface impact.
Finite canvas viewing extent clips hyperbolic paths. Fit view caps its contribution from each conic at 100000 km before margin; manual zoom extends farther.

Extreme repeated impulses and very long duration scenarios are outside the tested numerical envelope. Surface-crossing detection samples 15-second segments rather than analytically locating all conic intersections.
No reload persistence or runtime network access.
repairs: Removed an unnecessary invalid CSS import before validation. No numerical test failures or physics repairs were required.
